key_risks.title: Terra Carta weather ≠ curtailment
key_risks.body: AIG UK discloses one non-damage product — Terra Carta weather-index parametric covers at group level (trigger_gap 3/4, product_fit 1/4). UK energy cedants on physical-damage-led power and renewables programmes face basis risk when NESO constraint orders curtail output without insurable damage. Weather-index triggers do not track gate status or distribution curtailment — legacy BI wording leaves more spillover than Allianz's two disclosed non-damage products.

key_risks.title: Portfolio proxy HHI concentration
key_risks.body: Derived aggregation/correlation scores 3/4 effective (HHI 0.9348 over 46 mapped L3 assets across six boundary zones). AIG's 3% disclosed energy GWP share understates correlated UK grid stress if several renewable cedants in Scotland or East England constrain concurrently — accumulation models target nat-cat and machinery breakdown rather than man-made grid events.

key_risks.title: Engineering without grid telemetry
key_risks.body: Global Risk Engineering and Power Generation Risk Consulting provide site assessments and benchmarking (data_monitoring 2/4, pricing_modelling 2/4) but no disclosed curtailment-probability or connection-status model for UK renewables. AA- capital (4/4) and deep energy bench (underwriting_expertise 4/4) support earning_it posture, yet pricing-grade availability datasets remain absent — tier: assessed.

key_risks.title: Two BI products, no availability
key_risks.body: Allianz Commercial discloses two non-damage/parametric products (trigger_gap 2/4, product_fit 2/4) via expert BI articles, but neither is an availability-index or NESO-gate trigger for UK power cedants. Strategic Energy & Construction franchise (book_concentration 3/4 assessed) writes damage/BI on renewables and utilities — curtailment losses without physical damage still face basis risk versus Swiss Re Corporate Solutions red-weather parametric.

key_risks.title: Strong prep, unmodelled grid tail
key_risks.body: Preparedness 80/100 and AA group capital (4/4) give +14.8 margin-of-safety on earning_it quadrant, but aggregation/correlation 3/4 (portfolio HHI 0.9348) is register-derived not filing-quantified at cedant level. Allianz Risk Consulting exceeds generic statistics (data_monitoring 3/4) yet publishes no UK curtailment telemetry — correlated constraint episodes may be immaterial at group level but invisible until renewals.

key_risks.title: Scenario tools, no curtailment model
key_risks.body: Technical risk consulting and scenario tools on large industrial risks (pricing_modelling 3/4 assessed) exceed rule-of-thumb pricing but stop short of validated curtailment-probability methodology for UK renewables. Tenor mismatch 2/4 (5-year cover vs 3-year claims history) extends exposure against thin UK constraint-loss history — tier: assessed.

key_risks.title: Zero parametric on Energy desk
key_risks.body: Syndicate 2232 Property & Energy Europe/UK discloses zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4) — maximal basis-risk gap in the batch. Duncan Gorton's combined Property & Energy team writes damage/BI indemnity only; UK wind, solar and BESS cedants on non-firm connections have no availability or parametric cover from this carrier.

key_risks.title: Sidelined on preparedness axis
key_risks.body: Preparedness 35/100 and −16.0 margin-of-safety place Allied World in sidelined quadrant despite A+ capital (238% SCR). No published curtailment methodology (pricing_modelling 1/4), no energy telemetry (data_monitoring 1/4), and only 1% disclosed energy GWP (£3.9m/£472m) — underwriting relies on submission data and engineering benchmarks on a small but fully damage-led book.

key_risks.title: Portfolio HHI on tiny book
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation/correlation 2/4 (HHI 0.9348 over 46 L3 assets) flags correlated UK grid zones even though energy premium is immaterial at syndicate level. Propagated non-firm intensity 2/4 (I=0.1031) applies without public covered_assets on 2232 — tier: derived; close via register_pull on cedant placements.

key_risks.title: Parametric in ibott, not 1969
key_risks.body: Apollo Syndicate 1969 discloses zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4) on its oil-and-gas energy line; parametric innovation and data-science capability sit in sibling ibott/Syndicate 1971, not on the upstream franchise Stephen Portman and Matt Stubbings lead. UK grid-relevant cedants placed on 1969 get damage/BI only — basis risk on curtailment without damage.

key_risks.title: Standalone power out of appetite
key_risks.body: Disclosed energy GWP is USD 0.14m on USD 858m total (0% share) — standalone UK power generation is explicitly out of appetite. Named upstream bench (underwriting_expertise 3/4) covers O&G property and liability, not renewables or data-centre power — non-firm intensity 1/4 and aggregation 1/4 reflect minimal UK grid tail.

key_risks.title: Data-science without grid models
key_risks.body: ibott cites embedded actuarial and data-science functions (data_monitoring 2/4) but publishes no curtailment or connection-status methodology on Syndicate 1969 (pricing_modelling 1/4). A+ Lloyd's capital (4/4) supports sidelined posture (+2.6 MoS) — tier: assessed on analytics depth.

key_risks.title: 17% renewable book, no availability
key_risks.body: Ark Syndicate 4020 discloses 17% Marine & Energy GWP (£132m/£758m) covering wind, solar, hydro and BESS (book_concentration 3/4) with zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). Named renewable team (Mundin, Hill, Monk) writes conventional property damage/BI — UK cedants on non-firm connections face maximal basis risk; exposed quadrant at −25.2 margin-of-safety.

key_risks.title: BESS curtailment basis risk
key_risks.body: Ark's BESS and wind appetite sits on evidence-based underwriting philosophy without curtailment telemetry (data_monitoring 1/4) or published pricing methodology (pricing_modelling 1/4). Constraint-driven revenue loss on battery storage — Scotland and East England zones in portfolio HHI 0.9348 — is not a modelled peril; rule-of-thumb pricing on the £136m renewable franchise.

key_risks.title: Aligned tenor, weak prep
key_risks.body: Tenor mismatch 0/4 (3-year cover aligned to 3-year claims history) is a relative strength, but preparedness 45/100 reflects zero parametric capability against 70.2 exposure score. A+ capital (4/4) provides balance-sheet headroom that underwriting tools do not match — tier: disclosed on tenor, assessed on prep gap.

key_risks.title: kWh data is US-centric
key_risks.body: Aspen Specialty's renewed kWh Analytics partnership brings proprietary US renewable asset and loss databases (data_monitoring 3/4, pricing_modelling 3/4) but disclosed zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). UK Lloyd's energy cedants on the £42m (4%) energy class get quantitative US-informed pricing without UK curtailment telemetry or availability triggers.

key_risks.title: Physical-damage renewable gap
key_risks.body: Renewable energy coverage via kWh partnership is physical-damage-led; curtailment and constraint revenue loss without insurable damage falls outside disclosed product scope. Whitespace quadrant (+8.1 MoS) reflects moderate exposure (56.9) and decent prep (65) on a diversifying specialty book — basis risk persists on any UK non-firm cedant.

key_risks.title: A+ capital, unverified UK mix
key_risks.body: A+ Lloyd's capital (4/4) and Sompo group network support specialist renewable underwriting (underwriting_expertise 3/4), but UK cedant connection status on assumed treaties is not register-verified. Aggregation/correlation 2/4 (HHI 0.9348 portfolio proxy) — tier: derived; close via register_pull.

key_risks.title: Weather parametric ≠ availability
key_risks.body: Atrium's Quantitative Weather & Climate team and AUGold platform offer one disclosed non-damage product (trigger_gap 3/4, product_fit 1/4) — weather and climate parametric indices, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment orders. Upstream energy desk (Gault, Bond, Burrows) writes damage/BI on £1.1m energy GWP; UK power cedants hedged on Met Office indices may still face basis risk on grid-firmness losses.

key_risks.title: Dual bench, no combined product
key_risks.body: Credible upstream energy specialists and established Weather & Climate parametric bench coexist (underwriting_expertise 3/4) but no availability product bridges the two for UK power. Whitespace quadrant (+15.3 MoS) on minimal grid exposure — 0.1% disclosed energy share and non-firm intensity 0/4 effective — structural gap matters only if upstream cedants expand into UK renewables.

key_risks.title: AUGold strong, curtailment absent
key_risks.body: AUGold implies quantitative weather modelling on parametric lines but no published curtailment methodology on upstream energy (pricing_modelling 1/4). Tenor mismatch 0/4 (3-year cover vs 3-year history) aligns policy term to loss data — tier: disclosed on tenor, assessed on pricing gap.

key_risks.title: 16% energy, zero parametric
key_risks.body: Aviva GCS discloses 16% energy GWP (£52m/£317m via Probitas syndicate stamp) on renewables construction-through-operational programmes with zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). Exposed quadrant at −25.5 margin-of-safety — among the highest grid-relevant book concentrations in batch14 writing damage/BI only on UK wind, solar and BESS cedants.

key_risks.title: Seven-year cover, three-year history
key_risks.body: Disclosed max cover tenor 7 years vs 3 years claims history (tenor_mismatch 3/4, m=0.267) extends renewable policies beyond the UK constraint-loss record NESO publishes. Named UK Renewable Energy team underwrites on engineering experience (pricing_modelling 1/4 assessed) without curtailment-probability models — tail grid events may be underpriced relative to policy term.

key_risks.title: HHI proxy on concentrated book
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation/correlation 3/4 (HHI 0.9348 over 46 L3 assets) combined with propagated non-firm intensity 2/4 (I=0.1031) flags correlated UK constraint zones on a book where cedant-level connection status is not filing-verified. A+ capital (4/4) absorbs individual losses but portfolio grid stress is tier: derived.

key_risks.title: ExcessWeather ≠ curtailment index
key_risks.body: AXIS discloses one non-damage product — ExcessWeather index parametric weather catastrophe covers (trigger_gap 3/4, product_fit 1/4). Weather-index triggers capture meteorological events, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment — UK power and transition cedants on Syndicate 1686 or purpose-built Syndicate 2050 may face basis risk despite AXIS being the most availability-ready carrier in the batch.

key_risks.title: 2050 readiness, 1686 tiny book
key_risks.body: Syndicate 2050 led by Elliot Lyes targets energy transition (underwriting_expertise 4/4) but Syndicate 1686 discloses only 1% energy GWP (USD 17m/USD 1.97bn). Whitespace quadrant (+21.6 MoS, prep 71.2) reflects strong technical research (AXIS Explores downtime studies) against minimal current UK grid premium — capability exceeds deployed book.

key_risks.title: Research without curtailment model
key_risks.body: Published AXIS Explores failure and downtime studies inform renewable pricing (pricing_modelling 2/4, data_monitoring 3/4) but no formal curtailment-probability methodology is disclosed. Aggregation/correlation 3/4 (HHI 0.9348 portfolio proxy) and non-firm intensity 3/4 propagate without cedant register evidence — tier: assessed on models, derived on aggregation.

key_risks.title: O&G only, no renewables cover
key_risks.body: Horace Energy (Syndicate 4242) underwrites upstream oil-and-gas property and liability (7% energy GWP, USD 29m/USD 390m) with zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). Chris Charlton's specialist bench targets offshore and onshore O&G — UK grid-connected wind, solar and BESS are outside stated appetite despite exposed quadrant scoring (−18.7 MoS).

key_risks.title: Damage-BI with no telemetry
key_risks.body: Horace pages describe damage-and-BI energy covers only; no published asset monitoring, curtailment telemetry or pricing methodology (data_monitoring 1/4, pricing_modelling 1/4). Propagated non-firm intensity 1/4 reflects low grid relevance — any misclassified UK renewable placement would carry full basis risk on curtailment without damage.

key_risks.title: A+ capital, weak prep tools
key_risks.body: A+ Lloyd's capital (4/4) provides balance-sheet depth that preparedness 45/100 does not match — net-zero transition statement on Horace pages substitutes for quantitative grid-correlation modelling. Tier: disclosed capital, assessed prep gap.

key_risks.title: Casualty focus, not curtailment
key_risks.body: BHSI UK's 2021 Energy & Technical Lines Casualty team (Oliver Brown, Manager) writes energy-sector casualty and technical lines — not power-generation property where curtailment BI attaches (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). UK renewable and data-centre cedants seeking availability cover must look elsewhere; BHSI's franchise does not address grid-firmness revenue loss.

key_risks.title: AA+ sheet, exposed posture
key_risks.body: Strongest balance sheet in batch14 (AA+ FSR, capital 4/4) sits against exposed quadrant (−20.3 MoS, prep 45/100). No energy telemetry (data_monitoring 1/4) or curtailment pricing models (pricing_modelling 1/4) — Berkshire specialty culture relies on underwriter judgement without quantitative grid-correlation tools.

key_risks.title: Secondary energy, full trigger gap
key_risks.body: Energy is secondary to the wider BHSI specialty portfolio (book_concentration 2/4 assessed); propagated non-firm intensity 2/4 (I=0.1031) applies without public covered_assets. Any assumed UK power property exposure inherits maximal trigger gap — tier: assessed book mix, derived non-firm.

key_risks.title: Data-led, damage-only renewables
key_risks.body: Brit cites intelligent data use in energy underwriting and claims (data_monitoring 3/4) but discloses zero non-damage products on renewable energy pages (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). Dedicated upstream/downstream/renewables team writes conventional Lloyd's damage/BI — UK cedants on non-firm connections have no availability trigger despite data-driven prep (65/100).

key_risks.title: Tiny energy tail on £2.9bn book
key_risks.body: Disclosed energy GWP is USD 21m on USD 2.86bn total (1% share, book_concentration 0/4) — grid-relevant premium is immaterial at syndicate level. Whitespace quadrant (+15.6 MoS) reflects low exposure (49.4) against decent prep; correlated UK DC stress may be invisible in cedant-level monitoring until renewals.

key_risks.title: Experience pricing, no curtailment model
key_risks.body: Data-driven underwriting references (pricing_modelling 3/4 assessed) rely on Lloyd's market experience and engineering benchmarks without published curtailment-probability or connection-status models. Aggregation/correlation 2/4 (HHI 0.9348 portfolio proxy) — tier: assessed pricing, derived aggregation; close via entity_analysis.
